reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes Intelligent Dog as an arbitrage product claiming to allocate 6% to 18% monthly profit to users’ wallets and invites viewers to register through an app link and code. The presentation also offers referral income tied to sharing friends and their bitcoin entrustment. These are presented claims, not verified returns or completed transfers; the speaker says users retain private-key control, while the claimed Samsung-related affiliation is unverified.

opening.argument: The presentation includes material that cuts against treating the offer as a deceptive guarantee. It expressly warns that users must retain their private keys and that the platform does not provide password access or transaction rollback. It also depicts the risks of artificial arbitrage. The 6% to 18% figure is described as an allocation of arbitrage profit, not as proof that every user will receive a guaranteed return. On the supplied material, the speaker presents a risk-bearing digital-asset tool with explicit custody limitations, rather than concealing the conditions and risks of participation.

Only the User who controls the private key can control the assets of the corresponding Account.
about 6% to 18% of the monthly profit allocation to your wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited profit language identifies a share of arbitrage profit, but it does not itself establish a guaranteed outcome, a completed transfer, or concealment of risk. The prosecution also emphasizes private-key control while omitting that the presentation expressly says password recovery and rollback are unavailable. Referral examples likewise do not prove that any recruitment or payment occurred.

citations.quote: The Plus Token does not provide access to the password, transaction rollback, and so on.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The private-key warning describes custody, not the reliability of the promoted returns. The speaker still tells viewers that Intelligent Dog allocates 6% to 18% monthly profit and presents layered bitcoin income. Calling the figure an allocation does not make the advertised opportunity merely educational or remove its persuasive financial promise.

opening.argument: The material can reasonably be read as an animated technology explanation and product demonstration. It explains how the robot is intended to identify price differences across trading platforms, describes storage and blockchain recording, and illustrates the account and robot through diagrams and a mock interface. The supplied frames show explanatory animation rather than a visible completed transaction flow. That presentation supports interpreting the video as commentary about a proposed digital-asset system and its operating model, not as verification that a particular viewer has earned money.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats an explanatory account of a tool as if it were proof of misconduct. The robot description explains intended operation, while the animation does not purport to document a completed user result. Even the referral calculations are presented as examples within the explanation, so their presence does not establish that the video is primarily a deceptive solicitation.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Technical explanation and animation do not neutralize the direct invitation and benefit claims. The presentation tells viewers they can delegate arbitrage, receive monthly allocations, and earn link revenue from friends. Those are promotional claims about participation and income, not just neutral instruction about how blockchain systems work.

opening.argument: At most, the material promotes an identifiable digital wallet and trading service with an associated referral promotion. The supplied evidence does not establish a deposit being made, a credential being requested, a completed withdrawal, or a real commission payment. Instead, the speaker says the user controls the corresponding assets through the private key and describes storage and transactions as recorded on the blockchain rather than on the platform server. The examples of bitcoin income therefore remain illustrations of the proposed service's referral terms, not proof of a scam mechanism.

rebuttal.rebuttal: A download link and referral terms are consistent with promotion of a digital service, but they do not establish that the service took deposits or paid fictitious returns. The prosecution's quoted examples describe hypothetical entrustment and calculations; they do not show an actual transfer. The evidence also affirmatively describes user-controlled private keys rather than a request to surrender credentials.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a shown completed transfer does not change what the speaker is asking viewers to consider. The service is promoted with a download link, monthly arbitrage allocations, and commissions tied to friends' bitcoin entrustment. Private-key control addresses account custody, but it does not show that the promised returns or multilevel income are genuine.
